column2:
(Required)
Enter sample site name

Note: Multiple samples can be taken from the same immediate area and therefore have the same site name.

Enter "Lab site" for negative controls.
column3:
(Required)
Enter sample name. 

Please use unique values for each sample.
column4:
(Required)
Choose one of the following types from the dropdown: Sample, Negative control (a field or lab blank)
column5:
(Required)
Positive latitude values for north heading, negative for south. If no location is associated with a sample, enter a coordinate for the county or state where the samples were collected.  

Leave blank if a control. Optional for experimental samples (Examples: lab, aquarium).
column6:
(Required)
Positive longitude values for east headings, negative for west. If no location is associated with a sample, enter a coordinate for the county or state where the samples were collected.

Leave blank if a control. Optional for experimental samples (Examples: lab, aquarium).
column7:
(Required)
Enter the date associated with samples, not controls. 

Some common formats: mm/dd/yy, mm-dd-yy, yyyy-mm-dd

Leave blank if a control.
column8:
(Required)
Enter the name of sequencing technology used from one of the dropdown options.

Leave blank if not a sample.
column10:
(Required) 
Enter the adapter type. 
(Examples: TruSeq, Nextera)
column11:
(Required)
Enter the name of a target metabarcoding marker. There must be at least one marker described in this spreadsheet for each sample. 

If there are additional markers, each one should be entered separately by adding additional columns to the right (see columns N-P)
column12:
(Required)
Enter the FORWARD primer sequence used on the target marker gene. Make sure there are no spaces in the sequence.

There can be multiple rows where the same marker is used but different primers. Only published primer sequences are allowed. Here is a list of primers we currently support but more can be added on request.
column13:
(Required)
Enter the REVERSE primer sequence used on the target marker gene. Make sure there are no spaces in the sequence.

There can be multiple rows where the same marker is used but different primers. Only published primer sequences are allowed. Here is a list of primers we currently support but more can be added on request.
column14:
(Optional)
Use these columns and add others as as needed to include information about each additional marker used in your project. Change the number of the target marker name in the column header to be numbered Marker 2, Marker 3, etc...
column17:
(Optional)
Use these columns and add others as as needed to include information about each additional marker used in your project. Change the number of the target marker name in the column header to be numbered Marker 2, Marker 3, etc...
column23:
(Required)
Enter the name of the fastq file, from the sequencer, containing the forward reads. We will do all the processing for you. 

If you have multiple files, please concatenate them. Files should be gziipped. Filenames are needed to associate the samples with the metadata.
column24:
(Required)
Enter the name of the fastq file, from the sequencer, containing the reverse reads. We will do all the processing for you.

If you have multiple files, please concatenate them.Files should be gziipped.  Filenames are needed to associate the samples with the metadata.
column25:
(Optional) 
Enter in the sample substrate using one of the categories in this list or add your own.
(Examples: clay, gravel, ice, water)

Leave blank if a control.
column26:
(Optional)
Enter the number of liters filtered if this is a water sample.
Leave blank if a control.
column27:
(Optional)
Enter in the depth at which the sample was collected.

Leave blank if a control.
column28:
(Optional)
Describe the environmental features of this sample location using one of the options in this list or add your own. This describes the geographic features of the location where the sample was collected. You may add additional environmental feature columns as needed. 
(Examples: enclosed water, slope/slant, rocky shore)
